sections.heading: C2 — Mountain, night and adverse-weather driving
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Mountain, night and adverse-weather driving

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A111
If visibility conditions become too severe, leave the roadway and stop rather than creeping along where another vehicle may strike from behind. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A111
Avoid using emergency flashers while moving in poor conditions because another driver may mistake the vehicle for stopped. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A111
Reduce speed in wet weather because stopping takes more distance and quick turns can cause a skid. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A111
A light rain's beginning can be especially slippery when water mixes with road oil. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A111
Hydroplaning means the tires ride on a water film and can lose roadway contact and control for braking, acceleration or steering. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A111
To reduce hydroplaning risk, slow for rain, slush and standing water, replace worn tires and keep inflation correct. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A111
If entering a slippery area or beginning to hydroplane, keep a straight course and gently release the accelerator. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A111
Do not attempt an abrupt turn or stop while hydroplaning; wait for tire grip to return. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A111
If braking is necessary in the described slippery-area situation, the handbook advises gentle pumping for vehicles without ABS. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A112
Take immediate protective action after a Flash Flood Warning or when water is visibly rising fast. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A112
Do not drive across a flooded road; turn back and select another route. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A112
Leave flood-prone dips, low areas, canyons, dry creek beds and stream corridors for higher, safer ground. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A112
Avoid river, stream and already-flooded areas because an underwater road may have been damaged or washed away. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A112
If a vehicle stalls during the flood situation, leave it promptly and move to higher ground before rising water can sweep it away. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A112
Use added care at night when flooding hazards are harder to see. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A112
During threatening flood conditions, do not camp or park beside a stream or dry stream bed. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A112
The handbook warns that as little as six inches of fast-flowing water can knock a person down, and two feet can carry away a vehicle. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A113
On icy or snowy roads, drive slower, turn and stop gently and allow a longer following gap. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A113
Prepare lights, tires, brakes, wipers, defroster and radiator for winter use. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A113
Before even a short winter drive, clean and defrost the windows; keep the washer filled with nonfreezing fluid. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A113
Use the vehicle's fitted safety belts and shoulder restraints during winter travel. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A113
Start slowly to test steering and braking on winter roads, and press the accelerator gently to avoid wheelspin. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A113
The winter guidance says to begin slowing for a turn or stop at least three times sooner than usual. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A113
When stopping on slick winter roads, avoid sudden steering; consult the owner's manual, using gentle brake pumping for non-ABS vehicles and steady pressure when appropriate for ABS. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A113
The handbook recommends tire chains for very slippery roads and checking other states' winter chain rules before traveling there. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A113
Watch for ice in shade and on bridges or overpasses, where it may form earlier or persist longer. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A114
The handbook's usual studded-snow-tire interval is October first through April thirtieth, with possible department changes for weather. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A114
Carry a winter emergency kit in case a breakdown or crash strands the vehicle. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A114
The kit list includes a flashlight and spare batteries, first-aid supplies, a pocket knife and at least one blanket or sleeping bag. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A114
Pack extra gloves, socks, a wool cap, traction sand or cat litter and a small shovel for winter stranding. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A114
Include water, booster cables, emergency flares, nonperishable food, a bright attention cloth, waterproof matches or a lighter, a local map and a phone charger. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A114
Before running the engine for heat while stranded, ensure snow does not block the exhaust pipe. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A114
If available, attach a bright scarf or cloth to the antenna so snow crews can spot the stranded car. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0114]

ranked.label: Respond to rain, hydroplaning and flood danger
Use winter control and equipment guidance

corpus_stability.reason: Corpus is the frozen July handbook snapshot; future issuer changes require a new source registration, rather than silent updates to this corpus.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page one hundred eleven gives tire-grip examples at thirty-five and fifty-five miles an hour without complete tire, water-depth or road conditions. These are not taught as guarantees or hydroplaning thresholds.

The same page says maintain a steady speed and then slowly release the accelerator when approaching a slippery area or hydroplaning. The supported straight-line, gradual-release and no-sudden-stop/turn instructions are retained; the intended relation to steady speed needs clarification before teaching a combined speed prescription.

The bridge and shade icing explanation spans physical pages one hundred thirteen and one hundred fourteen. The local caution about those locations is covered; the complete causal explanation needs a multi-page binding.

The printed October-through-April studded-tire interval on physical page one hundred fourteen explicitly permits department weather adjustments. No adjustment for the current season has been checked; the printed default must not be presented as verified current-season permission.

The illustrative stream-width, depth and growth-time values on physical page one hundred twelve lack the conditions needed for a predictive model. They are withheld; no water depth is represented as safe to cross.
